sentences.text: Rahul Dhiman vs State Of Uttarakhand on 8 November, 2024

Author: Ravindra Maithani
Bench: Ravindra Maithani
 High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital
 1st Bail Application No. 1377 of 2024
 Rahul Dhiman ........Applicant
 Versus
 State of Uttarakhand ........Respondent
 Present:-
 Mr. Bharat Singh, Advocate for the applicant.
 Mr. Vipul Painuli, Brief Holder for the State.
 Mr. Pranav Singh, Advocate for the informant.

entities.text: High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)

Applicant Rahul Dhiman is in judicial custody in Fir No. 327 of 2024, under Sections 306, 498A
Ipc and Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, Police Station Kotwali Roorkee, District
Haridwar.
He has sought his release on bail.

2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
3.
The deceased and the applicant were married on 19.02.2017.
FIR records that after marriage, the deceased was harassed and tortured by the applicant and his family members for and in connection with demand of dowry.
On 15.05.2024, the informant was told that the deceased has died.
FIR records that she was killed.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that according to the prosecution, it is a case of suicide.
He would submit that the applicant had no fight or quarrel with the deceased; the deceased was staying with the parents of the applicant; at the time of incident, the applicant had gone for his work.
He would submit that there is no abetment to suicide.

5. Learned counsel for the informant would submit that it is not a case of abetment to suicide;
instead it is a case of murder.

He would submit that the deceased was harassed for dowry demand;
the deceased was taken by the applicant on 12.05.2024; the deceased had told her sister through text messages that the applicant and his family members are doing "natak" with her.
6. Learned State Counsel would submit that the witnesses have supported the prosecution case.
He would submit that the applicant had demanded dowry from the mother of the deceased and not from the father of the deceased.

sentences.text: 7. It is a stage of bail.
Much of the discussion is not expected of.
Arguments are being appreciated with the caveat that any observation made in this order shall have no bearing at any subsequent stage of the trial, or in any other proceeding.
8. Just after 7 years of marriage, the deceased has committed suicide.
The Court does not want to comment on the demand of dowry.
The informant has stated that the demand was not made from him but was made from the deceased telephonically, which he overheard.
What abetment was made to the deceased to commit suicide?
This and many more questions would fall for deliberation during trial.
9. Having considered, this Court is of the view that it is a case fit for bail and the applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
10. The bail application is allowed.

11. Let the applicant be released on bail, on his executing a personal bond and furnishing two reliable sureties, each of the like amount, to the satisfaction of the court concerned.
(Ravindra Maithani, J) 08.11.2024 Avneet/
